Sidious recalled Tarkin's prosecution at Ahsoka's trial as harming the relationship between Anakin Skywalker and then-Admiral Tarkin, and surmised that despite the Jedi's transformation into a [[Dark Lord of the Sith]], Darth Vader still harbored resentment against Tarkin for his treatment of his former Padawan.<ref name="Tarkin">[[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']]</ref>

[[File:Ahsoka_sees_a_hologram_of_Anakin.png|thumb|right|250px|Ahsoka sees a hologram of Anakin.]]
During her time with the Spectres, Tano was stationed aboard the ''Phoenix Home'' when the Rebel fleet was attacked by the Sith Lord Darth Vader. During the battle, Tano sensed the anger and hatred emanating from the dark sider, and she was met with the realization that the individual behind Vader's mask was Skywalker. The incongruity of the two men being the same caused Tano to lose consciousness. In the aftermath of this discovery, Tano struggled to accept the truth. Although she maintained that she was unaware of the Sith Lord's identity,<ref name="Siege of Lothal" /> she secretly harbored feelings of grief and guilt, haunted by the idea that she could have helped her master in his time of need. During a mission to the Jedi Temple on Lothal, Tano was confronted by a vision of Skywalker that preyed upon these fears, blaming her for allowing Darth Vader to rise. Tano fought back against the vision, believing that there was still a way to reach her master.<ref name="Shroud of Darkness" />

[[File:DuelOnMalachor-DV.png|thumb|left|300px|Ahsoka met her former master and dueled him.]]
Upon finally coming face-to-face with her former master once again on Malachor, Tano refused to believe that he and Vader were the same person; she was unable to reconcile the Sith Lord's vile nature with the kindness of the man she once knew. Although it pained her, Tano viewed Vader as the murderer of Anakin Skywalker and vowed to avenge her master's death, going against the Jedi teachings she had learned as a child. She battled him atop the Sith Temple, defending the Padawan Ezra Bridger. As the Temple began to collapse, Tano damaged Vader's mask, revealing the scorched face of Skywalker. The sight of her master forced her to pause. Feeling the guilt from leaving him years ago, Tano refused to leave Vader and continued to duel as her friends escaped.<ref name="Twilight of the Apprentice" /> Before the debris of the ceiling could crush them both, Tano destroyed the floor beneath them, causing Vader to fall.<ref name="A World Between Worlds" />

====After Anakin's death====
In [[4 ABY]], Anakin returned to the light side of the Force and sacrificed his own life to defeat Darth Sidious at the [[Battle of Endor]].<ref name="Galactic Atlas" /> Following her master's death, Tano reflected on the impact of Anakin's decisions on the galaxy. Despite his flaws, she remembered him as "the best of us," a good man who fell victim to his own fears,<ref name="Chapter 13" /> and had favorable things to say about him.<ref name="BOBF6" /><ref name="218 Ahsoka" /> In 9 ABY,<ref name="The Mandalorian Date" /> she refused to train the youngling Grogu because she recognized that the child's attachment to his father figure Din Djarin made him vulnerable to the same fears as Anakin. Tano could not bring herself to separate the infant from Djarin, vowing to not set him down the same self-destructive path as her old friend. However, she relented and told Djarin of Tython, a place where Grogu could reach out with the Force to contact other Jedi if he chose to.<ref name="Chapter 13" />

Unsurprisingly, given her close relation to the Skywalker family,<ref name="218 Ahsoka" /> Tano met Anakin Skywalker's son Luke Skywalker at some point. In fact, when asked how she knew of his temple, she only answered that she was an old friend to the Skywalker family. Tano and Skywalker were on good terms. She even advised him in the training of Grogu, such as telling the young Skywalker to trust his instincts, and accepted his decision to train the youngling despite her own lack of desire to do so. She would even declare that being by Skywalker's side was the safest place in the galaxy for a young Force-sensitive like Grogu.<ref name="BOBF6" /> While she still did not consider herself a Jedi,<ref name="CEUAEK">''[[Star Wars: Character Encyclopedia, Updated and Expanded Edition]]''</ref> she had faith that Skywalker would create a "great school" and kept Djarin from seeing Grogu, as per Jedi rules on attachment.<ref name="BOBF6" /> She favorably referenced Anakin to his son<ref name="218 Ahsoka" /> by noting they were similar and did not rule out seeing Luke again.<ref name="BOBF6" /> In the World Between Worlds, Anakin appeared to Tano as his younger self to complete her training.<ref name="Part Five" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|During the Clone Wars, I worked with a lot of people. I fought alongside clones, who took orders from me even though I lacked their experience. I watched politics on a dozen different worlds. I helped train people who'd never held a blaster in their lives. When I did all that, I had the Jedi to back me up, but I think I could do almost as good a job with you.|Ahsoka Tano, to Bail Organa|<ref name="Ahsoka" />}}
===Lightsaber abilities===
{{Quote|I admit, Ahsoka's a little rough around the edges, but with a great deal of training… and patience… she might amount to something.|Anakin Skywalker, on Tano|audio=AhsokaRoughEdges-TCWf.flac|<ref name="TCWFilm" />}}
Ahsoka Tano made use of an unorthodox reverse grip during combat, but, at the insistence of her master, eventually began to utilize the standard grip<ref name="Preview Special">[[Dave Filoni]] in [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''The Clone Wars'']] Preview Special</ref> in addition to her reverse grip.<ref name="Shattered" /> Tano was a particularly acrobatic lightsaber duelist who often utilized the Force to jump down on her opponents and to dodge lightsaber strikes. Although she was physically smaller than many of her foes, she proved to be a skilled duelist, wielding one and eventually two lightsabers.<ref name="Twilight of the Apprentice" /><ref name="TPA" />

At the beginning of her apprenticeship under Skywalker, Tano's combat skills were already quite considerable given that she defeated three IG-100 MagnaGuards single-handedly during her first mission.<ref name="TCWFilm" /> Later, Tano temporarily held her ground against the skilled Sith assassin Asajj Ventress<ref name="Cloak of Darkness" /> and the Jedi hunter General Grievous after only a very short time training under Skywalker, although she was forced to run away from Grievous a short time into their confrontation.<ref name="Duel of the Droids" /> Her skills in lightsaber combat developed over time,<ref name="A Necessary Bond" /> and she began to favor using a variant of Form V in battle<ref name="Ahsoka & Padme" /> like her master,<ref name="Anakin Skywalker Product Description">{{FantasyFlightGames|url=en/products/star-wars-legion/products/anakin-skywalker-commander-expansion|text=Anakin Skywalker Commander Expansion}}</ref> although Offee was certain she would be skilled at Form VI as well.<ref name="Ahsoka & Padme" />

[[File:Ahsoka-Tano-Carlac.png|thumb|right|300px|While still an apprentice, Tano became a practitioner of Jar'Kai, which she used for years.]]
During the Clone Wars, Tano became a practitioner of [[Jar'Kai]], wielding a yellowish-green shoto lightsaber in addition to her standard lightsaber. However, Tano occasionally utilized only her main lightsaber, such as when she dueled Skywalker on Mortis while under the dark side influence of the Son. Nevertheless, Tano more commonly utilized Jar'Kai, particularly when facing multiple opponents such as when she engaged the much more experienced Skywalker and Kenobi on Mortis.<ref name="Altar of Mortis" /><ref name="FB">{{Facebook|username=DaveFiloni|url=notes/dave-filoni/qa/10150219391017571|name=[[Dave Filoni]]|date=2011-03-23|archivedate=20160101103626|archivefile=File:DaveFiloniQA-Facebook.png}}</ref> Whilst fleeing from clones after being framed for murder, Tano lost her second lightsaber and was forced to use only her main lightsaber to fight Barriss Offee. Her duel against Offee showed that she had become too reliant on her second lightsaber, something she had in common with Asajj Ventress, and though she did put up a considerable fight, Offee overwhelmed her.<ref name="To Catch a Jedi" />

Around two years after<ref name="509 Date note">{{TCWcanondates|509}}</ref> her first duel with Grievous, Tano proved during their encounter on Florrum that her skills in lightsaber combat had improved vastly as she held her own against all four of Grievous's lightsabers,<ref name="A Necessary Bond" /> whereas previously she only lasted a short time when he was using only two lightsabers. Instead of fleeing after exchanging only a few blows,<ref name="Duel of the Droids" /> Tano held her ground and gave the Younglings time to escape before escaping with them.<ref name="A Necessary Bond" /> By the time of the Siege of Mandalore, Tano demonstrated highly advanced skills in lightsaber combat as evidenced by her prolonged duel with the powerful former Sith Lord Maul. Although Maul successfully disarmed Tano at the conclusion of their duel, she turned Maul's own attack against him in order to defeat him nonetheless.<ref name="TPA" />

[[File:AhsokaTano-SWTLC.png|thumb|left|250px|Tano wields her white lightsabers during her adult life.]]
Throughout the Clone War, Tano showed adeptness with deflecting blaster shots, particularly during Order 66, where she survived in a prolonged battle against her own men.<ref name="Victory and Death" /> Even in extremely close-quarter fighting, she was able to defend herself despite being surrounded by multiple troopers.<ref name="Shattered" /> Thanks to her training, she knew she could fight while blinded, yet she recognized needing to do that and fight without lightsabers would be a challenge. She was also skilled enough to fight without lightsabers, defeating the Sixth Brother, who was wielding a lightsaber, with only the Force.<ref name="Ahsoka" />

Sixteen years after her departure from the Jedi Order, Tano's skill in lightsaber combat had greatly improved to the point of mastery. During a skirmish at Hammertown, she easily defeated two Imperial Inquisitors at once and even deactivated the double-bladed [[Seventh Sister's lightsaber|lightsaber]] of the Seventh Sister with her bare hands.<ref name="The Future of the Force" /> During the mission to Malachor, Tano again proved capable of fighting several Inquisitors at once and even disarmed the Fifth Brother and destroyed his lightsaber. During the same mission, Tano again proved capable of dueling to a stalemate with the former Sith Lord Maul before breaking off the fight to rescue Ezra Bridger. Shortly afterward, Tano engaged in an intense duel with Darth Vader, and although she ultimately lost, she proved capable of putting up a much more impressive fight against him than either Jarrus or Bridger were previously able to.<ref name="Twilight of the Apprentice" />

===Force powers===
{{Quote|Because of Ahsoka's advanced abilities, I forgot how young she is.|Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="Holocron Heist" />}}
[[File:AhsokaForcePush-TA.png|thumb|right|250px|Ahsoka Force pushes a Pyke Guard into a wall.]]
Gifted with raw Force skill,<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> Tano at first was only skilled at sensing the intentions and emotions of those around her, although she was able to advance in more skills once her training began.<ref name="Ahsoka" /> She was noted by her master to possess advanced abilities.<ref name="Holocron Heist" /> At the beginning of her apprenticeship, Tano was capable of telekinetic feats as evidenced during the Battle of Christophsis, where she pulled down a large wall in order to save Skywalker from a group of retail droids. In another instance, Tano strongly [[Force push|pushed]] Ventress and flung her back some distance in order to save the life of Luminara Unduli.<ref name="Cloak of Darkness" /> By the end of the Clone Wars, Tano's telekinetic abilities advanced to the point that she was able to hold Maul aloft high above the city of Sundari<ref name="TPA" /> and could use the Force to prevent a small starship from taking off. During Order 66, she was able to use the Force to guide her two lightsabers in a circle to cut an escape path for her and Rex.<ref name="Victory and Death" /> Tano later proved able to create a powerful protective [[Force barrier]] that was capable of temporarily holding back fiery dark side energies conjured by Darth Sidious.<ref name="A World Between Worlds" />

Tano also had a strong ability to sense things in the Force, feeling the presence of Plo Koon after his fleet was destroyed by the ''Malevolence''<ref name="Rising Malevolence" /> and the presences of the children who were kidnapped by Cad Bane.<ref name="Children of the Force" /> She also eventually learned how to perform mind tricks.<ref name="The Academy" /><ref name="Sphere of Influence" /> Tano would sometimes use a Force choke, despite it being a dark side Force power, but relied on it mostly to temporarily fend off an enemy. She used this method against a Trandoshan hunter on Wasskah, prompting her companion Kalifa to use it as well. However, when Kalifa did not let go and began to threaten to kill the hunter, Tano convinced her to let the Trandoshan go, saying it was not the Jedi way to kill out of anger.<ref name="Padawan Lost" />

In addition, Tano's Force powers enabled her to leap to incredible heights. She used this to her advantage when leaping into the ''Phantom'' in order to escape two Inquisitors.<ref name="The Future of the Force" /> She frequently used her acrobatic prowess during lightsaber combat, using front flips, back flips, and somersaults to avoid enemy attacks. During a duel against General Grievous, she vaulted herself on top of the cyborg general before springing off his back and escaping.<ref name="Bond" /> Ultimately, thanks to her skill in the Force, she was never weaponless, as she could always call upon its power.<ref name="Ahsoka" />

[[File:AhsokaHand2Hand-GWaT.png|thumb|left|300px|Tano was skilled in hand-to-hand combat.]]
Tano also experienced Force visions and dreams. She used the Force to heal two corrupted kyber crystals that had been "bled red" and restored them to their natural white color. These crystals became part of her new twin lightsabers. Tano was also able to use the Force to amplify her touch. On one occasion, she used this Force power to shatter the hilt of the Sixth Brother's double-bladed spinning lightsaber.<ref name="Ahsoka" />

Tano also demonstrated the ability to sense the thoughts and feelings of others. When she met [[Din Grogu|Grogu]], Tano was able to sense his thoughts to such a precise degree that she was able to deduce his name and that he had been trained as a Jedi youngling at the Temple on Coruscant.<ref name="Chapter 13" /> Tano possessed the rare ability known as [[psychometry]], which allowed its users to learn the history related to an object by coming into contact with it.<ref name="Part Five" />

===Other abilities===
{{Quote|When I was out there, alone, all I had was your training and the lessons you taught me. And because of you, I did survive. And not only that, I was able to lead others to survive as well.|Ahsoka Tano, to Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="Wookiee Hunt" />}}
In addition to her Force powers and lightsaber combat skills, Tano was a talented pilot and also displayed skill as a war strategist by leading an attack that penetrated a Separatist blockade on Ryloth.<ref name="Storm Over Ryloth" /> During the Clone Wars, Tano passed on some of her flight knowledge to Senator Amidala, instructing her in starfighter combat.<ref name="The Starfighter Stunt" /> Due to her piloting skills, Tano found work as a courier for the Fardi clan while on the run from the Empire. She believed her skill in flying came from being trained by Anakin Skywalker, whom she considered the best pilot in the galaxy.<ref name="Ahsoka" />

Tano displayed skill in hand-to-hand combat, as she easily overpowered Cad Bane before dropping her guard and being incapacitated by the bounty hunter.<ref name="Children of the Force" /> She later used her hand-to-hand combat skills on Mandalore by single-handedly defeating a group of the Mandalorian Secret Service and later holding off several guards and subduing Prime Minister Almec despite being handcuffed. However, on that occasion, she armed herself with one of the guards' shields, which she used to fend them off and defend herself from a stun gun.<ref name="The Academy" /> While she was a prisoner of Trandoshan hunters, Tano killed the hunters Dar and his father, Garnac, by only using hand-to-hand combat and her Force powers.<ref name="Padawan Lost" /><ref name="Wookiee Hunt" />

[[File:JediShuttle634EngineCompartment-GOM.png|thumb|right|250px|Just like her master, Tano was a very capable mechanic]]
Tano had a considerable knowledge of mechanics, which she had learned from her master. She used her mechanical skills to contact Skywalker and save her and Barriss Offee's lives when they were trapped under a destroyed droid factory on Geonosis. She also knew how to repair vehicles. While on Mortis, she repaired the shuttle that she, Kenobi and Skywalker had crashed on the planet.<ref name="Weapons Factory" /><ref name="Ghosts of Mortis" /> Tano later used her skills as a mechanic as her occupation after Order 66 and the fall of the Republic, repairing starships and threshers while hiding on Thabeska and Raada. Tano assembled her new twin lightsabers from scrap metal parts she had acquired from the Fardis.<ref name="Ahsoka" />

Tano understood Shyriiwook, as demonstrated by her translations for Chewbacca while captured on Wasskah.<ref name="Wookiee Hunt" /> During their mission to Malachor, Tano was able to read some words in [[Ur-Kittât]], the ancient Sith [[language]].<ref name="Twilight of the Apprentice" /> Tano also was an effective military tactician, as well as a good leader and teacher.<ref name="Join the Battle" />

==Equipment==
===Weapons===
{{Quote|Two lightsabers, you have. Two, you shall use.|Yoda, to Ahsoka while she was learning to use two blades at once|<ref name="Teach You" />}}
[[File:Ahsoka_Tano_Lightsaber_DB.png|thumb|left|150px|Ahsoka's first lightsaber]]
{{Main|Ahsoka Tano's lightsabers}}
{{Main|Ahsoka Tano's white lightsabers}}

Ahsoka Tano owned two different pairs of lightsabers. She originally built her first lightsaber, which had a silver cylindrical hilt and a green blade, before becoming Anakin Skywalker's Padawan at the Battle of Christophsis.<ref name="TCWFilm" /> She wielded this lightsaber by itself for some time, before constructing a shoto lightsaber with a matching hilt and a yellow-green blade to accompany it upon taking up Jar'Kai.<ref name="Overlords">{{TCW|Overlords}}</ref> Both sabers had kyber crystals from the sacred planet of Ilum.<ref name="Ahsoka" /> Tano wielded both lightsabers in battle until her departure from the Jedi Order, upon which the weapons fell into the care of her former master Skywalker. While they were in his custody, Skywalker tinkered with them to improve them, which led to the sabers having blue blades when he returned them to Tano before the start of the Siege of Mandalore.<ref name="Old Friends" /> Tano would later abandon the sabers on a [[moon]] after the issuing of Order 66<ref name="Victory and Death" /> in order to fake her death to the Empire.<ref name="Ahsoka" />

[[File:AhsokaTano-TMUSC.png|thumb|right|200px|Ahsoka wielding her white-bladed lightsabers]]
Over a year after the Clone Wars, Tano constructed a new pair of lightsabers, these ones with white blades, during the evacuation of Raada. The weapons initially had rough handles made of pieces of scrap Tano had acquired on her journeys, although she later rebuilt the hilts to be more functional and decorative. The kyber crystals within, as well as their mountings, came from the lightsaber of the Inquisitor Sixth Brother, whom Tano had defeated on Raada. Tano found the crystals familiar, and speculated they had been looted from the Jedi Temple after the Order's fall. After claiming the crystals, she purified them of the taint of the dark side until they shone white before assembling the weapons with scrap materials she had collected.<ref name="Ahsoka" /> These white lightsabers continued to serve her during the early rebellion, as she used them in battle against multiple Inquisitors, as well as Darth Vader.<ref name="The Future of the Force" />

During her time on Thabeska in the first year of the Empire, Tano also owned a unidentified blaster model which she used against Stormtroopers while escaping the planet of Thabeska. She destroyed it in order to provide a diversion for her escape. When her starship was captured by Chardri Tage and Tamsin, agents of Bail Organa, after her second departure from Thabeska, Tano knocked them out with a pair of [[baston]]s she had selected from the ship's weapons box.<ref name="Ahsoka" />

===Attire===
{{Quote|R7, take over the ship. I'm going after Anakin. Somebody has to save his skin.|Tano, before exiting her interceptor on Cato Nemoidia|<ref name="Sabotage" />}}
[[File:AhsokaEta2.png|thumb|left|250px|Ahsoka piloted an Eta-2 ''Actis''-class light interceptor near the end of the Clone Wars.]]
During her time as a Padawan, Tano flew two different [[Jedi starfighter]]s. At Ryloth and Umbara, Tano flew [[Ahsoka's Delta-7B Jedi Starfighter|her own]] [[Delta-7B Aethersprite-class light interceptor|Delta-7B ''Aethersprite''-class light interceptor]].<ref name="Storm Over Ryloth" /><ref name="Darkness on Umbara" /> Later, while fighting in the defense of the planet Cato Neimoidia, she [[Ahsoka Tano's Eta-2 Actis-class interceptor|piloted]] a newer [[Eta-2 Actis-class light interceptor|Eta-2 ''Actis''-class light interceptor]],<ref name="Sabotage">{{TCW|Sabotage (episode)}}</ref> in what would be her last battle before leaving the Jedi Order.<ref name="The Wrong Jedi" /> Both starfighters sported dark red paint jobs with a white Jedi symbol over the top of it, and were co-piloted by her personal astromech droid, [[R7-A7]].<ref name="Storm Over Ryloth" /><ref name="Sabotage" />

Tano often flew missions with Anakin Skywalker in the Corellian [[G9 Rigger-class light freighter|G9 ''Rigger''-class light freighter]] ''Twilight'' in the earlier stages of the Clone Wars, including at the [[Battle of Teth]],<ref name="TCWFilm" /> the [[Battle of Abregado]],<ref name="Rising Malevolence" /> the [[Raid on Skytop Station|Mission to Skytop Station]],<ref name="Duel of the Droids" /> and the [[Mission to Mustafar (Skywalker and Tano)|Mission to Mustafar]].<ref name="Children of the Force" />

After her departure from the Jedi, Tano purchased a Joben T-85 speeder bike that was so prone to breaking down, Trace Martez dubbed it "Trash" when asked to name it.<ref name="Gone with a Trace" /> Tano left the bike with the [[Martez family|Martez sisters]] at their repair shop when she left to search for Maul with Bo-Katan Kryze, saying that she would come back for it.<ref name="Together Again" />

Upon her first departure from Thabeska, Tano stole a small and unremarkable freighter from the Fardi clan, which she used to travel around before and during the occupation of Raada, as well as when she returned to the Fardis.<ref name="Ahsoka" /> Tano flew an [[A-wing starfighter]] on missions during the early rebellion, including to Takobo.<ref name="The Future of the Force" /> Following the battle of Endor, Tano traveled to Lothal in a T-6 shuttle to meet her friend Sabine Wren.<ref name="Family Reunion – and Farewell" />

===Outfits===
====Typical garb====
{{Quote|Much growth you have shown, Ahsoka Tano. On the path to becoming a Jedi Knight, you are.|Master Yoda, before bestowing Tano with a Padawan braid extension|<ref name="The Padawan Path" />}}
[[File:AhsokaTano2-TCWLD.png|thumb|right|250px|Ahsoka's first outfit she wore as a Padawan]]
When she initially became a Padawan, Tano wore a dark red bandeau top and skirt with white tights, along with dark red boots and fingerless gloves, as well as a purple sash.<ref name="TCWFilm" /> Tano later changed to wearing a dark red backless dress at the same time as she built her second lightsaber, this time with grey tights with diamond-shaped cut-outs and armbands with diamond shapes on her upper arms.<ref name="Heroes on Both Sides" />

She also wore a beaded headdress with a Padawan braid made of silka beads behind her right front lekku;<ref name="TCWFilm" /> after a ceremony on Coruscant, Master Yoda granted her an extension to the braid.<ref name="The Padawan Path" /> The braid was taken away from her on two occasions: once briefly when she was captured by Cad Bane during the Battle of Devaron,<ref name="Cargo of Doom" /> and the other when she was expelled from the Jedi after being framed for treason. She was offered the braid back after her name was cleared, but chose to leave the Order instead.<ref name="The Wrong Jedi" /> Ahsoka also had a wrist-mounted comlink but she had to destroy it to lay low while being on the run.<ref name="To Catch a Jedi" />

[[File:AhsokaBonteriEstate.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Ahsoka's second outfit worn in the later years of the Clone Wars]]
After surviving Order 66, she donned a hood that covered her face and montrals to obscure her identity.<ref name="Victory and Death" /> During her time on Thabeska and Raada, Tano wore a nondescript outfit, the only clothing she owned at the time. It was occasionally accompanied by hoods that concealed her face, with fellow Togruta Selda giving her a new one that fit her recently grown montrals better. She also owned a disused weapons belt that she put to use again upon constructing her second pair of lightsabers, and was given a backpack on Raada that didn't rub against her lekku.<ref name="Ahsoka" />

When Tano met the Spectres after the naval action at Mustafar, she wore a grey dress with grey-and-brown armor plating on her chest and skirt, along with grey detached sleeves and forearm armor, as well as fingerless gloves. The outfit also had armored boots.<ref name="Fire Across the Galaxy" />

While operating on the planet Corvus during the [[New Republic Era]], Tano wore sleeveless dark blue robes and a large belt from which she hung her lightsabers, as well as a pair of silver vambraces and arm wrappings on her forearms. Tano draped a dark cloak over these clothes during her assault on Calodan. This cloak hid her amid the smog of Corvus and also doubled as a [[poncho]]. Although Din Djarin incinerated this cloak upon meeting the Togruta, she replaced it not long after with a similar covering.<ref name="Chapter 13" />

====Specialized clothing====
[[File:AhsokaTCWs7-AG.png|thumb|right|180px|Ahsoka's outfit worn during the Siege of Mandalore]]
During the boarding of Cad Bane's flagship in the Devaron system, Tano wore a dark red vacuum-sealed bodysuit and space helmet.<ref name="Cargo of Doom" /> When she participated in the [[Battle of Mon Cala]], Tano wore a grey-and-red scuba suit, with a face mask that allowed her to breathe but left her montrals and lekku exposed to the water.<ref name="Water War">{{TCW|Water War}}</ref> During the [[Mission to Zygerria]], undercover as a slave, Tano wore a turquoise outfit with gold jewelry and sandals, initially covered with a grey-purple body-covering robe.<ref name="SOTR" /> Tano also owned a reddish-grey winter coat lined with white fur, which she wore on cold planets such as Carlac and Ilum.<ref name="A Friend in Need" /><ref name="The Gathering">{{TCW|The Gathering (episode)}}</ref>

During her time wandering Coruscant after leaving the Order, Tano wore a light blue mechanic's jumpsuit, along with a brown headpiece that went over her montrals and between her lekku and had a grey raised diamond on the front. She also carried a brown satchel.<ref name="Gone with a Trace" /> After being recruited by Bo-Katan Kryze and her resistance group to help pursue Maul, Tano was given a new combat outfit consisting of a blue-and-grey dress with a short skirt, blue tights, and grey boots, as well as forearm armor and fingerless gloves.<ref name="Old Friends" /> The outfit also had Mandalorian beskar plating.<ref name="OFNF Episode Guide" /> After Order 66, she donned a grey cloak over that outfit.<ref name="Victory and Death" />

During the mission to rescue Janard, Tano wore an ocean jumpsuit.<ref name="Ocean" /> While fighting off Morgan Elsbeth's agents in the Denab system, Tano wore a blue spacesuit to survive the vacuum while directly defending against incoming starfighters.<ref name="Part Three">{{Ahsoka|Part Three: Time to Fly}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
===Overview===
{{Quote|I've always known that Ahsoka is bigger than just me. I think my hope for anyone that joins Team Tano moving forward is that they realize how much Ahsoka means to people and that she's more than just a character. She's more than just a role. She's more than just another story. Ahsoka is changing lives. I hope that whoever joins the team recognizes that and continues to breathe life into her in a way that carries on her legacy.|Ashley Eckstein|<ref name="Ahsoka Oral history">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2020/04/ahsoka-tano-clone-wars-finale-star-wars|text=Ahsoka Tano—A Star Wars Oral History|author=Breznican, Anthony|date=2020-04-24|work=[[Wikipedia:Vanity Fair (magazine)|''Vanity Fair'']]|archivedate=20200424215049}}</ref>}}
[[File:DisneyPlusAvatarAhsokaTanoTCW.png|thumb|left|250px|Ahsoka Tano, as represented through an icon for [[Disney+]] users]]
Ahsoka Tano was voiced by [[Ashley Eckstein]] in the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series and [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|film]],<ref name="TCWFilm" /> as well as in the following ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' television series.<ref name="Fire Across the Galaxy" /> Eckstein later authored the young-readers book ''[[Star Wars: I Am a Padawan]]''<ref name="I Am a Padawan">''[[Star Wars: I Am a Padawan]]''</ref> and narrated the [[Ahsoka (audiobook)|audiobook]] of the novel [[Ahsoka (novel)|''Ahsoka'']].<ref name="Ahsoka audiobook">[[Ahsoka (audiobook)|''Ahsoka'' audiobook]]</ref> American actress [[Rosario Dawson]] portrayed Tano in "[[Chapter 13: The Jedi]]," the fifth episode of ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'' [[The Mandalorian Season Two|Season Two]], with [[Caitlin Dechelle]] serving as a stunt double. This was the first live-action appearance of the character.<ref name="Chapter 13" /> Dawson continued to play Tano in the ''[[Star Wars: Ahsoka]]'' television series.<ref name="Announcement">{{SW|url=news/future-lucasfilm-projects-revealed|text=Future Lucasfilm Projects Revealed}}</ref>

Tano and several other ''The Clone Wars'' characters were featured within [[Lucasfilm]]'s [[2009]] holiday greeting card, which was designed by artists [[Kelly Smith]] and [[Harrison Parker]]. Tano and the others were depicted as ginger beard cookies. She was later featured within Lucasfilm's 2022 digital holiday card. Holding a cup of [[hot chocolate]], she and several others, including Obi-Wan Kenobi and Yoda, warmly welcome Darth Vader to a holiday party.<ref name="Holiday Card">{{SW|url=news/lucasfilm-holiday-cards|text=From Santa Yoda to Rocket Sleds: Lucasfilm's ''Star Wars'' Holiday Cards Through the Years|date=2022-12-22}}</ref>

===Development===
{{Quote|[George Lucas] said, 'This is going to be Anakin Skywalker's padawan because I want him to have a padawan. People don't expect that and it will add a way to give him somebody to teach, and it creates a great dynamic between him and Obi-Wan and her.' And at first it seems like, well that's a far-out idea.|Dave Filoni, discussing the development of Ahsoka Tano|<ref name="Ahsoka Oral history" />}}
[[File:SWTCW-poster.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Ahsoka Tano teased in shadow in an early poster for ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'']]
Early in ''The Clone Wars''{{'}} development, the character who became Ahsoka Tano was very involved in the [[black market]] and worked with Jedi without getting involved in the Clone Wars. She would try to prevent criminals from taking advantage of the war. Supervising director [[Dave Filoni]] and<ref name="Ahsoka Oral history" /> executive producer<ref name="Ambush">{{TCW|Ambush}}</ref> [[George Lucas]] decided that including a Padawan was important, and Lucas wanted her to be Anakin Skywalker's Padawan. He explained that she would give Skywalker someone to teach and her inclusion would create a dynamic between her, Skywalker, and Obi-Wan Kenobi. As of [[2005]],<ref name="Ahsoka Oral history" /> the character was named Ashla, a reference to an early name for the [[light side of the Force]] when Lucas was developing [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'']], and later canonized as the [[Lasat]] name of the Force.<ref name="Lasat-Gallery">{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/legends-of-the-lasat-trivia-gallery|text="Legends of the Lasat" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Slide 2}}</ref> Ashla is also the name of one Togruta Jedi youngling who appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']].<ref name="DB Bear">{{Databank|bear-clan|Bear Clan}}</ref> Filoni played with the idea of them being the same character, but he realized the ages would not work.<ref name="Ahsoka Oral history" /> The two characters, however, are otherwise unrelated.<ref name="Leland Ashla">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=1755#17143245|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Leland Y Chee]]|date=2008-02-18|time=1:47 PM|quote=No. The ages don't match up.}}</ref>

Lucas replaced the name "Ashla" with "Ashoka" after [[Wikipedia:Ashoka|Ashoka the Great]], the [[Wikipedia:India|Indian]] Emperor of the [[Wikipedia:Maurya Dynasty|Maurya Dynasty]]. [[Henry Gilroy]] then tweaked it to "Ahsoka" to make her name unique.<ref name="Henry Gilroy">{{Twitter|HGilroy67|status/1019372713712893952|[[Henry Gilroy]]|quote=In honor of #CloneWars 10th, the title page for the series bible I wrote back in 05. When we met with George to discuss the bible he changed Anakin's Padawan from 'Ashla' to 'Ashoka', after the Indian Emperor of the Maurya Dynasty. I later tweaked it to Ahsoka to make her unique.|archivefile=File:HenryGilroy-Ahsoka-July-18-2018.png}}</ref> Ahsoka Tano was one of the first characters that Filoni drew when he was working at Lucasfilm,<ref name="Ahsoka Oral history" /> inspired by San, the female wolf-riding protagonist of the 1997 [[Wikipedia:Hayao Miyazaki|Hayao Miyazaki]] and [[Studio Ghibli]] film [[Wikipedia:Princess Mononoke|''Princess Mononoke'']].<ref name="Mononoke">{{SW|url=news/swco-2017-11-things-we-learned-from-dave-filoni-and-pablo-hidalgos-animated-origins-and-unexpected-fates-panel|text=SWCO 2017: 11 Things We Learned from Dave Filoni and Pablo Hidalgo's "Animated Origins and Unexpected Fates" Panel}}</ref> Ahsoka's facial markings were partially inspired by those of San.<ref name="Insider 118">{{InsiderCite|118|Red Five|Red Five: Dave Filoni}}</ref> The character was revealed on [[January 29]], 2008, on [[StarWars.com]],<ref name="firstlook">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/news/news20080129.html|text=Padawan Ahsoka Joins the ''Star Wars'' Cast}}</ref> along with toy industry shows.<ref name="This Week! Ep1">{{ThisWeek|Li4auBiXm_0|Star Wars: The Clone Wars, The Child, Star Wars Nite, and More!|sw_url=video/star-wars-the-clone-wars-the-child-star-wars-nite-and-more}}</ref>

[[File:Ahsoka-PP.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Ahsoka Tano's younger appearance]]
Producer [[Catherine Winder]] felt ''The Clone Wars'' crew was fortunate in finding Eckstein, as she felt the actress naturally embodied the character.<ref name="SW:TCW Blu-Ray Commentary">The [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]] Blu-ray Creative Conversation commentary</ref><ref name="SW:TCW DVD Commentary">The [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]] DVD audio commentary</ref> Eckstein recorded the show's [[The Clone Wars: Season One|first season]] before the film premiered in [[2008]]. She had many conversations with Filoni, and she spoke with Lucas about their hopes for Tano and her journey in the series.<ref name="Ahsoka Oral history" /> Ultimately, Tano's story,<ref name="Skywalker: A Family at War" /> particularly the events surrounding her decision to leave the Jedi Order,<ref name="TCW4">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Four|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Four]]</ref> became a major part of Skywalker's own story and, ultimately, his fall to the dark side.<ref name="Skywalker: A Family at War" /> Indeed, Filoni himself noted as such in the "Obi-Wan Undercover" featurette for [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Four|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Four]]: in teasing the story of Tano leaving the Jedi, he noted [[The Clone Wars: Season Five|Season Five]] included a story that helped explain why Skywalker believed the Jedi Order had betrayed his trust.<ref name="TCW4" /> However, even though there were ideas for her to die during ''The Clone Wars'', Filoni did not want Tano's character to just exist as another factor that pushed Skywalker to the dark side. He figured that, if Tano only existed to be part of Skywalker's story, she would have been included in the films.<ref name="Ahsoka Oral history" />

===''The Clone Wars''===
Tano started out very young and naive because of the way the show was written, the crew's own naiveness, and their lack of experience.<ref name="Ahsoka Oral history" /> As "[[Downfall of a Droid]]" was initially the second episode to be developed for the ''Clone Wars'' series, Ahsoka's maneuver when attempting to fly between the Separatist frigates would've explained Anakin's hesitance for her to fly in the later produced episode "[[Shadow of Malevolence]],"<ref name="DoaD Episode Guide">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/downfall-of-a-droid-trivia-gallery|text="Downfall of a Droid" Trivia Gallery}}</ref> although "Shadow of Malevolence" would later be revealed to take place prior to "Downfall of a Droid."<ref name="Clone Wars Chronology">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-clone-wars-chronological-episodeorder|text=''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Chronological Episode Order}}</ref> Ahsoka's visions within the ''Clone Wars'' episode "[[Assassin (episode)|Assassin]]" were made to have the same distorted effect as her master Anakin's did in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]. In an early version of the script for the episode, Ahsoka visited the young bounty hunter Boba Fett in his [[Republic Judiciary Central Detention Center|prison cell]] in an attempt to learn information upon his former ally Aurra Sing.<ref name="Assassin EG">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/assassin-trivia-gallery|text="Assassin" Trivia Gallery}}</ref>

[[File:SWEAhsokaTano.png|thumb|right|250px|Ahsoka Tano's character model was updated to showcase her growth and increased maturity.]]
Ahsoka's model was updated for [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|''The Clone Wars'': Season Three]] to suggest time had passed,<ref name="New Look">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/newcharacterlooks/index.html|text=A New Look for ''The Clone Wars'' Heroes}}</ref> further showcasing that she had grown older, more mature, and more experienced. The updated character model debuted in the episode "[[Heroes on Both Sides]]."<ref name="HoBS Episode Guide">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/heroes-on-both-sides-trivia-gallery|text="Heroes on Both Sides" Trivia Gallery}}</ref> The update was first teased to fans in an announcement article on [[StarWars.com]]—which revealed a screenshot of Tano and Skywalker's updated models and a promotional image of the two of them with Kenobi in his own updated model—on [[November 16]], [[2010]]. Also included was a link<ref name="New Look" /> to a promotional video showcasing the three new models in action, featuring Tano leaping to the ground before her two mentors and igniting both her lightsabers.<ref name="New Look in Action">{{SWArchive|url=video/view/001152.html|text=New Character Models}}</ref><ref name="New Look in Action Backup">{{YouTube|video=LT9LwclXPfo|text=''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'': Season 3: New Character Models|channel=jbjsaltbox|name=Jason Jones}}</ref> While Kenobi and Skywalker's updates brought their designs closer to their appearances in ''Revenge of the Sith'', ''The Clone Wars'' crew had to work around the lack of any live-action reference for Tano, but her character development was as noticeable as any other cast member's: as Filoni explained to StarWars.com in the announcement article, Tano had much to learn at the start of the war, but she had grown and changed, which was reflected in her older, more mature appearance. Furthermore, he promised "Heroes on Both Sides" was yet another step forward in her emotional journey as she met Separatists face-to-face.<ref name="New Look" />

For the ''Clone Wars'' episode "[[Ghosts of Mortis]]," the model for Ahsoka's [[goggles]] was repurposed from the one used for Hondo Ohnaka's [[pirate]] gang.<ref name="GoM Episode Guide">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/ghosts-of-mortis-trivia-gallery|text="Ghosts of Mortis" Trivia Gallery}}</ref> In the ''Clone Wars'' episode "[[Citadel Rescue]]," Saesee Tiin's starfighter was modeled with the same pattern as Ahsoka's starfighter.<ref name="Citadel Rescue EG">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/citadel-rescue-trivia-gallery|text="Citadel Rescue" Trivia Gallery}}</ref> When Wilhuff Tarkin enters Ahsoka's cell in the ''Clone Wars'' episode "[[The Jedi Who Knew Too Much]]," it is framed as a homage to when Darth Vader enters Leia Organa's cell aboard the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] in ''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope''. Similar to this, his interaction with her while in her cell was meant to mirror his interaction with Leia shortly before he commands the [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|destruction of Alderaan]]. Ahsoka's leap from the water pipe in the ''Clone Wars'' episode "The Jedi Who Knew Too Much" is an homage to a similar scene in [[1993]] film ''[[Wikipedia:The Fugitive (1993 film)|The Fugitive]]''.<ref name="JWKTM EG">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/the-jedi-who-knew-too-much-trivia-gallery|text="The Jedi Who Knew Too Much" Trivia Gallery}}</ref> When Filoni and the crew were writing the story about Tano leaving the Jedi Order, they made it about her being pulled in different directions and becoming frustrated. They wanted to show young people that they can take a predetermined path or use the information to make their own choice.<ref name="Ahsoka Oral history" />

===''The Clone Wars'' cancellation and revival===
[[File:Ahsokawalkabout.png|thumb|left|300px|Ahsoka, as she appeared in a story reel that eventually became the episode "Gone with a Trace."]]
Following the cancellation of ''The Clone Wars'' in [[2013]], Filoni revealed that he had planned out [[The Clone Wars Legacy#Unfinished Episodes|twelve more episodes]] that continued Ahsoka's story. He described each four-episode arc at [[Celebration Europe (2016)|Celebration Europe]]. With the release of the seventh season of ''The Clone Wars'' in [[2020]], eight of the twelve episodes Filoni mentioned were fully completed.

In the first arc, Ahsoka would find a new way of life in the underworld of Coruscant and get close to a scoundrel called [[Nyx Okami]]. This arc eventually became the seventh season episodes "[[Gone with a Trace]]," "[[Deal No Deal]]," "[[Dangerous Debt]]," and "[[Together Again]]."<ref name="Reels">When comparing the reel shown in the {{SWYouTube|lS4sclln5J4|Ahsoka's Untold Tales Panel | Star Wars Celebration Europe 2016}} to the opening of "[[Gone with a Trace]]," it is clear that the reel footage was eventually developed into this episode.</ref> In the final release, several major changes were made to the arc, most notably the replacement of Nyx Okami with the Martez sisters, Trace and Rafa.<ref name="Gone with a Trace" />

[[File:AhsokaSithTemple-Concept.png|thumb|right|200px|Ahsoka being shocked by Darth Sidious' force lightning]]
The second arc, which was never completed, would have dealt with Ahsoka helping the Jedi Order and traveling beneath the Jedi Temple to a [[Shrine in the Depths|Sith shrine]]. The arc begins with Tano returning to warn the Jedi of a threat she discovered in the underworld of Coruscant.<ref name="Ahsoka's Untold Tales">{{SWYouTube|lS4sclln5J4|Ahsoka's Untold Tales Panel | Star Wars Celebration Europe 2016}}</ref>

Thereafter, Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker enlist her help to rescue Yoda from the Sith shrine underground. During this journey, Ahsoka and Anakin would have flown [[Wikipedia:Autogyro|autogyro]]-style vehicles and encountered large beasts resembling ''[[Wikipedia:Kaiju|Kaiju]]''. At some point during the arc, Ahsoka would protect the Jedi [[Holocron Vault]] from Darth Sidious, who would shoot [[Force lightning]] at her through the vault's doors.<ref name="Ahsoka's Untold Tales" />

[[File:AhsokaVsMaul-TPA.png|thumb|left|300px|Ahsoka Tano faces off against Maul in Season Seven's completed Siege of Mandalore arc.]]
The last planned arc centered around the Siege of Mandalore and was released fully as the episodes "[[Old Friends Not Forgotten]]," "[[The Phantom Apprentice]]," "[[Shattered]]," and "[[Victory and Death]]."<ref name="Old Friends" /> The color of Ahsoka's lightsabers in this arc changed during development. In the initial story pre-cancellation, the lightsabers were meant to have their original green hue, while the final version released in 2020 had a blue hue, reflecting changes that Anakin Skywalker made while the sabers were in his care.<ref name="OFNF Episode Guide" /> For the character's duel with Maul in the [[The Clone Wars: Season Seven|''The Clone Wars'': Season Seven]], stuntwoman [[Lauren Mary Kim]] provided motion caption work to portray Tano's acrobatic fighting style.<ref name="TPA" />

===''Rebels'' continuation===
[[File:AhsokaHS_Rebels.png|thumb|right|250px|Ahsoka Tano in ''Star Wars Rebels'']]
In the television series ''Star Wars Rebels'', Tano was meant to be a wandering [[Wikipedia:Samurai|samurai]],<ref name="Ahsoka Oral history" /> and she carried new, slightly curved lightsabers that are meant to resemble the weapons carried by samurai.<ref name="FAtG EG">{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/fire-across-the-galaxy-trivia-gallery|text="Fire Across the Galaxy" Trivia Gallery}}</ref>

Ahsoka's conversation with Rex in the ''Star Wars Rebels'' episode "[[Twilight of the Apprentice]]" is meant to mirror their first conversation in the ''Clone Wars'' film.<ref name="TotA EG">{{SW|url=series/episodes/twilight-of-the-apprentice-trivia-gallery|text="Twilight of the Apprentice" Trivia Gallery}}</ref>

In an interview with the official ''[[Star Wars]]'' website, ''Rebels'' co-creator and executive producer Dave Filoni stated that Vader wouldn't want a memory of Tano, a relationship that he considered a failure, and that he would be angry with her in a twisted way.<ref name="filoni">{{SW|url=news/interview-dave-filoni-on-star-wars-rebels-part-3|text=Interview: Dave Filoni on ''Star Wars Rebels'', Part 3}}</ref>

===Encounter with Bendu===
{{Quote|You are set on this confrontation then?''"<br />"''I have to know the truth.''"<br />"''So be it, but understand this, much will change as a result of this encounter, including you.''"<br />"''Isn't that true of all things, as time advances?''"<br />"''My dear, when I say change, I mean death.''"<br />"''So I will die?''"<br />"''Will you? I didn't know that. Goodbye then, Ahsoka Tano, former Jedi Knight.|Bendu and Ahsoka Tano, prior to Tano's confrontation with her former master|<ref name="Dave Filoni Tweet">{{Twitter|dave_filoni|status/883124880157192192|[[Dave Filoni]]|archivefile=File:AhsokaBenduMeeting.jpg}}</ref>}}
[[File:AhsokaandBendu.png|thumb|left|175px|Dave Filoni's artwork of Ahsoka meeting the Bendu.]]
After the conclusion of the third season of ''Star Wars Rebels'', series executive producer Dave Filoni revealed that Tano met the [[Bendu]] during the events of "[[The Mystery of Chopper Base]]." Though these events were never depicted on screen, Filoni tweeted dialogue from their encounter as well as artwork illustrating the event. During their conversation, Bendu mentioned Tano's upcoming confrontation with her former master. When Tano explained that she had to know the truth, Bendu retorted that everything would change as a result of their encounter, including her. As the Togruta failed to see his point, he specified that "change" meant death. Tano asked then if she would die, but Bendu acted as if she was affirming it, and so replied that he did not know that before telling her goodbye.<ref name="Dave Filoni Tweet" />

===''The Mandalorian'' and ''The Book of Boba Fett''===
{{Quote|I wanted to kind of have some [of Ahsoka Tano's] playfulness and her fun — the cocky eyebrow thing that she does. You know that she's got that feistiness. You know that she's willing to push the rules a little bit in order to get what needs to get done. But I also really like that she does have that wisdom. She's gone through a lot. She's really gone through a lot of things. And she's grounded, more than when you first meet her as a young teen. It was really fun to find moments to throw homages to the different aspects to Ahsoka that I've always loved.|Rosario Dawson|<ref name="Best of Jedi">{{SW|url=news/rosario-dawson-ahsoka-tano-interview|text=The Best of the Jedi: Rosario Dawson on Bringing Ahsoka Tano to Live-Action and ''The Mandalorian''}}</ref>}}
In [[February]], [[2017]], a ''[[Star Wars]]'' fan asked Dawson on [[Wikipedia:Twitter|Twitter]] if she would ever play Ahsoka Tano, and she replied that she would want to play her, causing fans to be excited about Tano appearing in live-action. According to Dawson, someone at Lucasfilm forwarded the Tweet to ''The Mandalorian'' executive producer Dave Filoni,<ref name="Best of Jedi" /> and he thought she would make a good Ahsoka Tano.<ref name="Tells all">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2020/11/rosario-dawson-dave-filoni-mandalorian-ahsoka-tano-grogu|text=Star Wars The Mandalorian: Rosario Dawson Tells All About Ahsoka Tano|author=Breznican, Anthony|date=2020-11-30|work=[[Wikipedia:Vanity Fair (magazine)|''Vanity Fair'']]|archivedate=20201207031817}}</ref> Filoni and ''Star Wars'' then followed Dawson on Twitter, but nothing happened for a long time.<ref name="Best of Jedi" /> Filoni kept loosely aware of Dawson's [[Wikipedia:Marvel Cinematic Universe|Marvel]] career and he watched interviews of her expressing excitement for the role.<ref name="Tells all" /> When Dawson and Filoni discussed the show, he revisited Dawson's casting and realized Dawson's age would fit Tano's age in the show, and he decided the casting was feasible. Filoni and ''The Mandalorian'' creator and executive producer [[Jon Favreau]] did not want to include Tano in [[The Mandalorian Season One|Season One]]<ref name="Best of Jedi" /> because Filoni did not want to mess up Tano's portrayal.<ref name="Ahsoka transformation">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-mandalorian-guide-to-season-two-exclusive-excerpt|text=Explore Ahsoka Tano's Transformation in ''Star Wars: The Mandalorian: Guide to Season Two'' – Exclusive Excerpt}}</ref>

During early production of Season One, Favreau told Filoni that the Child's name would be Grogu, prompting Filoni to think of ways the audience could learn his name. He thought that Tano could learn Grogu's name by communicating through memories and experiences, and she could tell this to the Mandalorian and the audience. Filoni and Favreau knew they wanted Tano in the [[The Mandalorian Season Two|second season's]] story, so they started visualizing Dawson in the role, and art of the actress playing Tano was created. After they showed that art to Dawson, they asked if she would take the role and she agreed.<ref name="Tells all" /> Concept designer [[Brian Matyas]] explained that the effects team shortened Tano's lekku due to practicality reasons when performing stunts.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.cbr.com/mandalorian-ahsoka-montrals-lekku-character-design|text=Mandalorian's Character Designer Explains Ahsoka's Shorter Montrals/Lekku|author=Wasserman, Ben|date=2020-11-29|work=[[Wikipedia:Comic Book Resources|''Comic Book Resources'']]|archivedate=20201201074637}}</ref>

Tano appeared in the episode Chapter 13: The Jedi, which was written and directed by Filoni.<ref name="Best of Jedi" /> According to Filoni, the episode was a test run to see how audiences would react to seeing Tano in live-action.<ref name="Ahsoka for life">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2022/05/rosario-dawson-ahsoka-tano-star-wars-series|text=''Star Wars'': Rosario Dawson Aims To Play Ahsoka Tano For Life|author=Breznican, Anthony|date=2022-05-20|work=[[Wikipedia:Vanity Fair (magazine)|''Vanity Fair'']]|archivedate=20220520134642}}</ref> When Filoni wrote the scene in which Tano reveals Grogu's history, he shaped it around when Obi-Wan Kenobi told Luke Skywalker about his father in ''A New Hope''. When Filoni was working on the episode, he knew the actress who plays the Magistrate would have to be someone who can instantly challenge Tano.<ref name="Tells all" /> After being cast as Tano, Dawson watched ''The Clone Wars'', ''Star Wars Rebels'', and the [[Star Wars saga|''Star Wars'' saga]] as preparation.<ref name="Best of Jedi" /> Dawson studied Ashley Eckstein's portrayal of Tano in animation and tried her best to honor it. Dawson was fascinated by how Tano was the center of "this whole other world" shown in ''The Clone Wars''. Dawson played Tano like a wandering [[Wikipedia:Samurai|samurai]] and a knowledgeable [[Wikipedia:Knight|knight]].<ref name="Tells all" /> Filoni pointed to [[Wikipedia:Gandalf|Gandalf]] from [[Wikipedia:The Lord of the Rings (film series)|''The Lord of the Rings'']] as a touchpoint, and all of this factored into Dawson's portrayal. Dawson wanted to have Tano's playfulness and fun, including her cocky eyebrow. She liked Tano's wisdom and how she is grounded after everything she has gone through. Dawson enjoyed having homages to the different aspects of Tano. Filoni talked about classic samurai films such as [[Wikipedia:Yojimbo|''Yojimbo'']], and he described Tano as someone wandering the galaxy helping people in need.<ref name="Best of Jedi" />

[[File:The_Mandalorian_Season_2_Ahsoka_Tano_Poster.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Ahsoka Tano character poster for ''The Mandalorian'']]
Many screen tests were done because the Volume tends to look magenta. Everything in Tano's costume was considered to an intense degree, including her headtails and horns. Filoni wanted Tano's facial markings to be subtle and look very natural instead of looking like face paint in ''The Clone Wars''.<ref name="Tells all" /> Makeup designer [[Brian Sipe]] had a difficult time finding the right look between human-realistic and pleasing to fans of ''The Clone Wars'' graphic image.<ref name="Ahsoka transformation" /> The crew tried to make Tano's makeup warm and natural, as well as have a different energy compared to animation.<ref name="Tells all" /> Dawson wanted to be as authentic to the animated Tano as possible, so she insisted on wearing blue contacts to match the character's eye color.<ref name="Best of Jedi" /> All of the prosthetics were built to Dawson's skull and body, and Tano's headband clipped in the back and held the headtails in place.<ref name="Tells all" /> The make-up artists tucked Dawson's hair away so she could wear the headpiece.<ref name="Ahsoka for life" /> The total transformation initially took three hours.<ref name="EW Rosario Natasha">{{OfficialYouTube|channel=@entertainmentweekly|name=Entertainment Weekly|link=Wikipedia:Entertainment Weekly|video=SNhSdfQI7Gc|text=Rosario Dawson and Natasha Liu Bordizzo on 'Ahsoka' | Star Wars Celebration | Entertainment Weekly}}</ref> Dawson thought the face markings, different skin color, and costume were incredible, but she did not feel like Tano until she put the contacts in. The crew had to worry about the Volume's temperature changing Tano's skin color, so small considerations were made and adjusted.<ref name="Tells all" />

Tano was again played by Dawson in "[[Chapter 6: From the Desert Comes a Stranger]]," the sixth episode of ''[[Star Wars: The Book of Boba Fett]]'' television series.<ref name="BOBF6" /> Dawson did not learn that her character would interact with Luke Skywalker until the day of filming. She was very excited that she got to work with [[Mark Hamill]],<ref name="Rosario Dawson Tweet">{{Twitter|rosariodawson|status/1507180811782549504|[[Rosario Dawson]]|quote=Are you kidding?! I was freaking out. I'm still pinching myself that I got to work with MARK HAMILL as AHSOKA. I didn't know my scene was with LUKE till day of...! @bobafett|archivedate=20220325171648}}</ref> who provided Skywalker's voice in the episode.<ref name="BOBF6" />

===''Ahsoka''===
{{Quote|Man, I am not a workout-y person, and I'm in my 40s getting into the most physically demanding role of my life. [Ahsoka's] not someone who gets tired. I can't play this like a human. She is an ''indefatigable'' alien. She's precise. She's master-level. The challenge is for me to show up and express that. It's like, I won't necessarily work out for myself, but I'll work out for Ahsoka any day of the week. I'm a huge fan, and I don't want to watch and be like, 'Yo, Ahsoka's hand seems a little shaky there.'|Rosario Dawson|<ref name="Ahsoka for life" />}}
[[File:ArianaRosario-Ahsoka.jpg|210px|thumb|left|Ariana Greenblatt and Rosario Dawson in costume as Ahsoka Tano.]]
Dawson continued to play Ahsoka Tano in the ''[[Star Wars: Ahsoka]]'' television series.<ref name="Announcement">{{SW|url=news/future-lucasfilm-projects-revealed|text=Future Lucasfilm Projects Revealed}}</ref> She rewatched the animated shows as preparation for reprising her role.<ref name="Rosario Natasha SWCA">{{SWYouTube|8RZiIf_oEAc|Rosario Dawson and Natasha Liu Bordizzo takes the stage at SWCA 2022 | Star Wars Celebration Live!}}</ref> Dawson cut most of her hair, leaving enough to be hidden comfortably under her headpiece.<ref name="Ahsoka for life" /> The makeup process had been reduced to an hour and a half while the whole transformation took about two hours. The process would start at 4:30 or 5:00 in the morning.<ref name="EW Rosario Natasha" /> Dawson wanted to show how Tano does not get tired, so she dedicated herself to intense lightsaber and fight training as well as studying Tano's past.<ref name="Ahsoka for life" /> Dawson and [[Natasha Liu Bordizzo]], the actress who played Sabine Wren, received [[Wikipedia:Chinese martial arts|wushu]] training from stunt coordinator [[Ming Qiu]]. Dawson showed Qiu freeze frames and clips from animated shows and asked Qiu to train her to do Tano's stunts. Qiu would say the stunts are not possible, but she showed Dawson what she could do instead.<ref name="Rosario Natasha SWCA" /> Dawson said this was the most physically demanding role of her life.<ref name="Ahsoka for life" /> She tried to show that Tano is struggling with balancing her humanity, experiences, and desires.<ref name="EW Rosario Natasha" />

A [[Ahsoka Season 2|second season]] of ''Ahsoka'' was announced to be in development on [[January 9]], [[2024]],<ref name="Mando Announcement">{{SW|url=news/the-mandalorian-and-grogu|text=''The Mandalorian & Grogu'' Journeys to the Big Screen}}</ref> with Filoni later revealing a development sketch on [[January 11]] that depicted Tano and Wren atop a statue of the Father,<ref name="Ahsoka Sketch">{{SW|url=news/ahsoka-season-2-dave-filoni-sketch|text=''Ahsoka'' Season 2 in Development, New Sketch Revealed}}</ref> a path previously braved by Baylan Skoll in the [[Ahsoka Season 1|season one finale]].<ref name="Part Eight">{{Ahsoka|Part Eight: The Jedi, the Witch, and the Warlord}}</ref> Ahead of season two, Dawson reflected on Tano's character arc in season one and her hopes for the upcoming episodes, specifically expressing hope for "some levity and some lightness" and calling back to Tano's "spunky energy" seen in her early ''The Clone Wars'' appearances. She also noted how Filoni compares Tano's journey to that of Gandalf's arc, a story in ''Lord of the Rings'' that sees an already-powerful and experienced wizard continue to grow and adopt a more joyful personality.<ref name="Levity and Lightness">{{WebCite|url=https://screenrant.com/star-wars-ahsoka-season-2-evolution-character-arc-rosario-dawson|text=Rosario Dawson Addresses Ahsoka's Evolution & Her Hopes For Season 2's Character Arc|author=Declan, Riz|date=2024-08-24|work=[[Wikipedia:Screen Rant|Screen Rant]]|archivedate=20240825183423}}</ref>

===Video game appearances===
[[File:SWFA_-_ahsoka-tano.png|thumb|right|250px|Ahsoka Tano in ''Star Wars: Force Arena'']]
Tano has appeared in various ''Star Wars'' video games. She could be deployed into battle in ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Defense]]''.<ref name="Galactic Defense">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Defense]]''</ref> She was playable as part of the player's team in ''[[Star Wars: Force Arena]]''<ref name="FA">''[[Star Wars: Force Arena]]''</ref> and is playable in ''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]''.<ref name="GoH">''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]''</ref>

Tano appeared as a playable character in the 2015 toys-to-life video game ''[[Disney Infinity 3.0]]'', which featured an original, but non-canonical, story set during the Clone Wars. Tano and her allies begin the story by learning a secret droid factory on Geonosis has been activated, kicking off a [[third battle of Geonosis]] and forcing the group to unravel who is behind a new Droid Army's creation. In the end, Tano and company would learn it was Maul's doing and engage the former Sith Lord in a battle on Naboo.<ref name="Infinity 3">''[[Disney Infinity 3.0]]''</ref> As part of ''Infinity''{{'s}} toys-to-life aspect, Tano was given her own figure that could be beamed into the game. In 2023, former ''Disney Infinity'' story lead [[Adrian Ropp]] revealed he had pushed for Tano to get her own figure despite reluctance on the part of higher-ups. He received support from the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] that ultimately cemented her place as a figure.<ref name="Ahsoka AMA 1">{{Twitter|toonbaboon|status/1691227826949947392|🎨[[Adrian Ropp|ToonBaboon]]📝|date=2023-08-14|quote=And we have a winner! This is one of my big reveals. I was the story person managing Star Wars content and guess who they didn’t want to make a figure of? Ahsoka!!! I had to fight tooth and nail to get that to happen and I got some much needed backup from the Lucasfilm… |archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/P4u81|archivefile=File:AdrianRopp-DisneyInfinityAhsoka-Twitter.png}} {{C|In response to: "What Star Wars characters didn't make the cut? If it's a big list, some big ones that were unknown to the public are good, just curious."}}</ref><ref name="Ahsoka AMA 2">{{Twitter|toonbaboon|status/1691228335362453504|🎨[[Adrian Ropp|ToonBaboon]]📝|date=2023-08-14|quote=…story team. I was one of a couple of people that passionately fought for a female character to be one of the playset pack characters. Holly, Jessie, Mrs. Incredible, Ahsoka, Gamora… so when girls played it they'd start with the choice!|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/P4u81|archivefile=File:AdrianRopp-DisneyInfinityAhsoka-Twitter.png}}</ref>

===Other appearances===
[[File:Acme-AhsokaJourney.png|thumb|left|300px|The life and journey of Ahsoka Tano, as depicted by artist [[Kayo Takahata]] in the piece "Ahsoka's Journey Continues"]]
Tano appeared in "[[Kamino Crisis]],"<ref name="CoK">{{LSWCite|101|Kamino Crisis}}</ref> a non-canon comic story written by [[Martin Fisher]] and published on [[October 7]], [[2023]]<ref name="jedi-bibliothek">{{WebCite|url=https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/lego-star-wars-magazin-101|text=LEGO Star Wars Magazin 101|archivedate=20240303173302}}</ref> in the [[LEGO Star Wars 101|101st issue]] of the magazine [[LEGO Star Wars (magazine)|''LEGO Star Wars'']]. In the comic, Anakin Skywalker, Tano and Clone Captain Rex were returning from a successful mission onboard the ''Resolute''. After Rex told them that their missions were too easy, the two Jedi planned to test the Captain by manipulating a training session for new clone troopers that was led by Rex. Tano disguised herself as a clone trooper named Tank, while Anakin Skywalker disguised himself as clone trooper Thrower to take part in a course in the [[Tipoca City Training Facility]] on [[Kamino]]. While they were fighting B1 battle droids that were repurposed as [[training droid]]s, a voltage peak caused the droids to become much more aggressive and skilled in combat.<ref name="CoK" />

The droids managed to break out of the training arena, after which Tano and Skywalker, still disguised as clone troopers, joined forces with Rex and other troopers to stop the rogue group of droids. While they were fighting in the hallways of [[Tipoca City]], the clone trooper [[Glider (clone trooper)|Glider]] went into the [[Control room (Tipoca City)|control room]] and destroyed the controls with his blaster, which caused the battle droids to be powered down. As Rex gathered the troopers to thank them, Tano and Skywalker took of their helmets and revealed themselves. They explained that they wanted to test the Captain and Rex responded that he wouldn't call their missions easy ever again. He then invited them to join his [[Rex's bowling team|bowling team]] if they ever left the Jedi Order.<ref name="CoK" />

Tano is depicted alongside Plo Koon on the cover of the ''[[Star Wars: Shatterpoint]]'' "First Contact" Mission Pack, which depicts both Jedi involved with a struggle against droidekas in a city environment during the Clone Wars.<ref name="First Contact">{{Asmodee|url=products/star-wars-shatterpoint-first-contact-mission-pack|text=Star Wars: Shatterpoint - First Contact Mission Pack}}</ref> It is unclear if this is meant to be taken as a canonical event.

===Contradictions===
====Height====
Carrying over information seen in Tano's entry on the [[StarWars.com]] [[Encyclopedia (StarWars.com)|Encyclopedia]],<ref name="SWE:Ahsoka">{{SWE|characters|ahsokatano|Ahsoka Tano}}</ref> Tano's initial entry on the StarWars.com [[Databank (2014-)|Databank]] in 2014—which at that time covered only the events of her teenage years in the initial run of ''The Clone Wars''—gave her height as 1.7 meters,<ref name="DB:AhsokaOldest">{{Databank|ahsoka-tano|Ahsoka Tano|oldversion=20140703012405}}</ref> which was then carried over as the height of the adult Tano seen in ''Star Wars Rebels''<ref name="DB:Ahsoka2017">{{Databank|ahsoka-tano|Ahsoka Tano|oldversion=20170706184708}}</ref> and ''The Mandalorian'' despite the obvious growth she had seen over the in-universe years.<ref name="DB:Ahsoka2020">{{Databank|ahsoka-tano|Ahsoka Tano|oldversion=20201207224646}}</ref>

Meanwhile, the [[2015]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]''<ref name="AEYNTK" /> and its [[2017]] update ''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know, Updated and Expanded]]'' listed the adult Tano's height as 1.88 meters, or 6 feet and 1 inches tall.<ref name="Absolutely Updated" /> The [[2021]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle!]]'' by [[Jason Fry]] affirmed that 1.7 meters, or five feet and seven inches, was Tano's height at some stage of her teenage years<ref name="Join the Battle" /> while that same year's ''[[Star Wars: Character Encyclopedia, Updated and Expanded Edition]]'' gave an adult height of 1.76 meters, or 5 feet, 9 inches.<ref name="CEUAEK" /> However, in 2023, her Databank entry was updated to reflect an adult height of 1.79 meters.<ref name="DB:Ahsoka2023">{{Databank|ahsoka-tano|Ahsoka Tano|oldversion=20230729214640}}</ref>

====Tales of the ''Ahsoka'' novel====
{{Quote|There isn't a big conspiracy behind the changes in Ahsoka's story. Dave approved the book six years ago and then kept working on her journey. It's frustrating to see people gleefully declare my book non-canon instead of just...using their imaginations. Like we did.|EK Johnston|<ref name="EK contradictions tweet">{{Twitter|ek_johnston|status/1553725660459417602|EK Johnston|quote=There isn't a big conspiracy behind the changes in Ahsoka's story. Dave approved the book six years ago and then kept working on her journey. It's frustrating to see people gleefully declare my book non-canon instead of just...using their imaginations. Like we did.|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/YNtZn}}</ref>}}
The ''Ahsoka'' novel by E. K. Johnston features a flashback to the Siege of Mandalore, in which Tano duels Maul in a plaza with green lightsabers before capturing him in a ray shield. After the execution of Order 66, which is implied to occur on Mandalore itself, Rex—who is suggested to already have had his inhibitor chip removed—and Tano fake their deaths by burying a [[Unidentified clone trooper (Rex's false grave)|clone trooper]] in Rex's armor and with her lightsabers. Rex then departs from the gravesite before Tano.<ref name="Ahsoka" /> These events were later overruled by the seventh season of ''The Clone Wars'', however.<ref name="TPA" /><ref name="Shattered" /><ref name="Victory and Death" /> An updated version of the novel was released that changed the color of Tano's lightsabers to blue, but the remaining contradictions were later left in place.<ref name="Ahsoka" />

The main plot of the novel sees Tano in hiding on the farming moon Raada under the name Ashla, only for her activity to be uncovered by the Sixth Brother Inquisitor, whom she slays before reuniting with Bail Organa.<ref name="Ahsoka" /> This series of events is also very similar to those depicted within the ''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (television series)|Tales of the Jedi]]'' episode "[[Resolve (episode)|Resolve]]," where the Inquisitor and farming site are not identified.<ref name="Resolve" /> Indeed, Dave Filoni stated that the ''Ahsoka'' novel and "Resolve" are the same story as "Resolve" is born from the same outline he had given to Johnston.<ref name="Nerdist">{{WebCite|url=https://nerdist.com/article/tales-of-the-jedi-dave-filoni-interview-ahsoka-tano-count-dooku-star-wars|text=Dave Filoni on How TALES OF THE JEDI Explores Choices Between Light and Dark|author=[[Amy Ratcliffe|Ratcliffe, Amy]]|date=2022-10-26|archivedate=20221026222129}}</ref> Johnston herself expressed a similar sentiment, claiming the ''Ahsoka'' novel and ''Tales of the Jedi'' episode could be the same events seen from the differing points of view of different creators.<ref name="JohnstonTempleGeek">{{YouTube|video=KgiFqFHA3fc|text=A conversation with author EK Johnston - Portrait of a Fangirl Podcast|channel=@templeofgeek|name=Temple of Geek|date=10-11-2023}}</ref> Before the episode's release, however, Johnston had theorized the book and episode depicted separate incidents. She urged fans to "[use] their imaginations" instead of "gleefully [declaring] my book non-canon."<ref name="EK contradictions tweet" />

Sources released since "Resolve" have seemingly attempted to separate it from the ''Ahsoka'' novel despite their similar plots. The 2023 reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Dark Side Pocket Expert]]'' reflects the Sixth Brother as appearing in novels and comics but makes no mention of him having been in ''Tales of the Jedi'' despite including information about the show elsewhere in its pages.<ref name="Dark Side Pocket">''[[Star Wars: The Dark Side Pocket Expert]]''</ref> The character then went onto appear in the 2023 novel ''[[Inquisitor: Rise of the Red Blade]]'' by [[Delilah S. Dawson]], whose text describes the Sixth Brother<ref name="Rise of the Red Blade">''[[Inquisitor: Rise of the Red Blade]]''</ref> as he appeared in ''Ahsoka'' and his comic appearances,<ref name="Dark Side Pocket" /> instead of adopting the appearance of the ''Tales'' Inquisitor.<ref name="Resolve" /> The [[2024]] reference book ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' then outright confirmed the ''Tales'' Inquisitor and Sixth Brother are separate characters by providing them separate entries. The book identified the ''Tales'' character as the First Brother,<ref name="SW Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]''</ref> a name quickly revealed to actually be intended for Marrok.<ref name="Discord">{{WookDiscord|discordname=.holocronkeeper|name=Leland Chee|date=2024-11-21|messagelink=https://discord.com/channels/397848917036761090/492457166771322881/1309008181808336926|quote=There was miscommunication and we got the number wrong in the Encyclopedia.|archivefile=File:LelandChee-Inquisitor-Discord.png}}</ref> The ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' article "[[Inquisitor Countdown]]" then revealed the ''Tales'' Inquisitor was named the [[Eleventh Brother]] and, again, separated him from the Sixth Brother.<ref name="Countdown">{{InsiderCite|229|Inquisitor Countdown}}</ref> While neither the ''Star Wars Encyclopedia''<ref name="SW Encyclopedia" /> nor "Inquisitor Countdown" reflect the events of ''Ahsoka'' in the Sixth Brother's description,<ref name="Countdown" /> this article takes the separation of both Inquisitors as proof that the events of ''Ahsoka'' and "Resolve" are separate, if similar, incidents.

The novel features Bail Organa first learning of Ahsoka Tano's survival of Order 66 a year into Imperial rule, while Tano is surprised to learn a known Jedi sympathizer like Organa is still alive.<ref name="Ahsoka" /> However, "Resolve" later revealed that he and Tano met during the funeral of Padmé Amidala.<ref name="Resolve" /> Therefore, the two must have both assumed the other died in the year between these events.

====Other matters====
[[File:SWR_Ahsoka_Gandalf.jpg|thumb|right|226px|Ahsoka Tano arrives on Lothal]]
The ''Rebels'' finale "[[Family Reunion – and Farewell]]" depicted Tano traveling to Lothal with white [[clothing]] and a matching [[staff]] on a T-6 shuttle to meet with Sabine Wren, who sought to bring Bridger home.<ref name="Family Reunion – and Farewell" /> This scene was later adapted for the ''Ahsoka'' series<ref name="Part 2 Highlights">{{SW|url=news/ahsoka-part-2-toil-and-trouble-highlights|text=''Ahsoka'' Analyzed: 5 Highlights from "Part Two: Toil and Trouble"}}</ref> with some changes, including Tano's clothing.<ref name="Part Two" /> This article assumes the most recent depiction—the version of the scene in ''Ahsoka''—is correct.

As a Padawan, Tano is featured on a variant cover for the [[Star Wars (2025) 5|sixth issue]] of [[Star Wars (2025)|''Star Wars'' (2025)]] by [[Alex Segura]]. Drawn by the artist "[[Bengal]]," the cover depicts Tano with Skywalker as representative of their time together as Jedi guardians. However, Tano—despite being depicted<ref name="SW2025 6">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/130734/star_wars_2025_6_variant/variant|text=Star Wars (2025) #6 (Variant)}}</ref> in her ''The Clone Wars'' seasons three<ref name="Altar of Mortis" /> through six attire<ref name="Destiny" />—is mistakenly depicted with a blue-bladed lightsaber,<ref name="SW2025 6" /> something she only wielded during the events of ''The Clone Wars'' Season Seven in her Mandalorian attire.<ref name="Old Friends" />
